veranderings.voor: Kos kan jou siek maak al lyk dit
veranderings.na: Kos kan jou siek maak, al lyk dit
veranderings.rede: A comma separates the main clause from the concessive 'al'-clause, between the two verbs.

veranderings.voor: en skraap nie net die skimmel af nie
veranderings.na: en moenie net die skimmel afskraap nie
veranderings.rede: A negative instruction in Afrikaans takes 'moenie'; 'skraap nie ... af nie' reads as a statement, not an instruction.

veranderings.voor: Jou neus en oë vang dikwels bederf
veranderings.na: Jou neus en oë merk dikwels bederf op
veranderings.rede: 'Vang' is an unnatural verb for noticing spoilage; 'opmerk' is the idiomatic choice and keeps 'dikwels' and 'gewoonlik'.

veranderings.na: of daaruit proe as dit opgeswel
veranderings.rede: One tastes the food from the tin, not the tin itself; 'daaruit' makes the object clear.

veranderings.voor: kos wat klaar is om te eet
veranderings.na: kos wat gereed is om te eet
veranderings.rede: 'Klaar is om te eet' echoes English 'ready to eat'; 'gereed' is the standard Afrikaans word here.

veranderings.voor: Gaar kos staan nie langer as twee uur buite nie
veranderings.na: Laat gaar kos nie langer as twee uur buite staan nie
veranderings.rede: The sentence is a rule for the learner but is phrased as a description; an instruction matches the surrounding imperatives.
'Los' for 'leave behind' is colloquial; 'agterlaat' is the standard written form.

veranderings.na: ver van kos af en nooit
veranderings.rede: The idiom for keeping something away from something is 'ver van ... af hou'.
A comma separates the subject clause 'Wat oorbly' from the main verb, between two verbs.

veranderings.voor: Siekte van kos met kieme, gif of bederf daarin noem ons voedselvergiftiging.
veranderings.na: As 'n mens siek word van kos met kieme, gif of bederf daarin, noem ons dit voedselvergiftiging.
veranderings.rede: The fronted object 'Siekte van kos ... daarin' is wooden; a conditional clause reads naturally with the same meaning.

veranderings.na: kry hulle nie noodwendig almal nie
veranderings.rede: 'Almal' on its own usually refers to people; 'hulle almal' clearly points back to the listed signs and symptoms.

veranderings.voor: neem die grootmens hom met die houer
veranderings.na: neem die grootmens die siek mens saam met die houer
veranderings.rede: 'Hom' has no clear antecedent after 'jy of iemand anders', and 'saam met' makes clear the container is taken along.

veranderings.voor: By kieme of bederf is 'n groot gevaar
veranderings.na: By kieme of bederf is daar 'n groot gevaar
veranderings.rede: The sentence lacks a formal subject; 'is daar' is required and leaves the protected 'n groot gevaar' intact.
A comma separates the main clause from the concessive 'al'-clause, between the two verbs.

veranderings.voor: bloed in die diarree of opgooi.
veranderings.na: bloed in die diarree of opgooisel.
veranderings.rede: 'Opgooi' is the verb; the substance in which blood is seen is 'opgooisel'.

veranderings.voor: Hulle gaan ook kliniek toe as hy nie beter word nie.
veranderings.na: 'n Grootmens neem hom ook kliniek toe as hy nie beter word nie.
veranderings.rede: 'Hulle' has no clear antecedent; the previous sentences name the adult as the one who takes the sick person.

vlae.teks: sonder om vir tekens te wag of hom te laat opgooi
vlae.rede: Not a language fault and not a safety flag: the protected entry says the pair 'tekens en simptome' must not be shortened to one word, and here 'tekens' alone may narrow the instruction (one should not wait for symptoms either). Changing it would alter meaning, so a writer or person should judge whether it is intended.
